payload.name: Preserve resolved relative times in event memories
payload.description: When a message states an event happened at a relative time (last week, yesterday, a few days ago), resolve it against the message/session timestamp and include the resolved time in extraction candidates and memory content.
content: During candidate extraction, if a message describes an event with a relative time expression (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday', 'a few days ago'), resolve it against the message/session timestamp and include the resolved actual date or period in the candidate's content and world_start.

When creating or updating event memories, keep the specific timing of an action distinct from the report date: if the message date is 14 August and the event occurred 'last week', record the event as occurring in early August rather than on the message date.
Do not drop temporal detail just because it is relative; preserve the resolved time so future questions about when the event occurred remain answerable.

solves: Event extraction can lose relative time phrases (e.g., 'last week') when recording memories, leaving later questions about when the event happened unanswerable. The rule: whenever a source message anchors an event with a relative time, resolve it against the message timestamp and preserve the resolved date/period in content and world_start. Applicable to any future construction where timing is expressed relationally; not needed for messages that already contain an explicit absolute date.
